newsitem.title: USA: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS HIGHER ON COMMERCIAL BUYING.
newsitem.headline: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS HIGHER ON COMMERCIAL BUYING.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures closed sharply higher on commercial buying, but stayed within their recent fairly narrow trading range, dealers said.
"I just think the market is in a trading range at the moment. Yesterday we hit the low end and tomorrow we may hit the high end," one floor trader said.

Dealers noted the key September contract had been drifting between $3.78 and $3.95-1/4 a bushel during the last two weeks. It closed on Tuesday up 9-1/2 cents at $3.90-1/4. Other months finished 9-3/4 to four cents higher.
Benson Quinn was a featured buyer of September both early and late in the session, dealers said.

There was some background talk that U.S. exports could pick up soon with the European Union appearing reluctant to issue export licenses. Egypt was among the potential buyers possibly set to tender shortly.
Volume was estimated at 16.8 million bushels, slightly higher than the previous day's 15.8 million.
